plugin.name: Narwal robot vacuum
plugin.author: Narwal plugin for Skypane
plugin.description: Shows and runs Narwal robot vacuums on your panels: the map with your rooms, live status and battery, vacuum or mop all rooms or the rooms you tap, pause, resume, send it home. Talks to the robot directly on your home network (no cloud, no app account). Works with Narwal robots that have local control (Flow, Flow 2, Freo Z10 Ultra, Freo X10 Pro).
settings.name: Name on the panels
settings.ipHelp: Your router's list of devices shows it. Give it a fixed address in the router so it doesn't change. There is no password: the robot's local port has none.
test.ok: Found it: a Narwal robot, software {firmware}, battery {battery}.
test.reach: No answer from that address. Check the address and that the robot is on, and close the Narwal app on your phone: the robot talks to one thing at a time.
refresh.ok: Asked for {n} map(s) again; the panels redraw when one changed.
err.noRobots: No robots yet: add one in Integrations, then pick it in this card's settings.
err.noRobot: Pick which robot this card shows (card settings).
card.name: Robot vacuum
card.controls: Start, pause and go home from this panel
card.station: Station buttons (wash mop, dry mop, empty bin)
rooms.tap: or tap rooms on the map
msg.offline: Can't reach the robot right now. Is the Narwal app open on a phone? The robot talks to one thing at a time.
msg.noMap: No map yet. The robot sends its map once it's online.
msg.notReady: The robot isn't ready (battery too low?)
fault.0x02310027: The right back wheel is stuck. Free it, then press Resume.
fault.0x01010072: The station is refilling its clean-water tank.
fault.generic: The robot needs help (code {code}). Check it, then press Resume.
settings.deviceIdPh: filled in by itself after a Test while it's cleaning
settings.deviceIdHelp: A docked robot doesn't say who it is. Start any clean (Narwal app, schedule or the robot's button) and press Test while it's cleaning: Skypane learns the ID and fills this in. Or paste the ID here if you know it (32 letters and digits).
test.needsId: Something answered at that address, but it hasn't said it's a Narwal robot. If it is your robot, it's asleep on its dock: start any clean (Narwal app or the robot's button) and press Test again while it's cleaning, or paste its Robot ID. If it still says this while the robot is cleaning, the address is probably wrong.
test.wrongId: The robot answered, but not to that Robot ID. Clear the Robot ID field and press Test while the robot is cleaning.
test.badId: A Robot ID is 32 letters (a–f) and digits. Clear it to let Skypane learn it.
msg.noId: Waiting for the robot to say who it is: start any clean once (Narwal app or its button), or add its Robot ID in Integrations.
